facts.fact: The National Population Commission commenced nationwide digital registration of births and deaths under its electronic civil registration and vital statistics system, operational on the VitalReg platform from 1 July 2026, on the account of its federal commissioner for Kogi.

Digital registration of births and deaths became operational nationwide on 1 July 2026 through the VitalReg platform, the National Population Commission's federal commissioner for Kogi told a briefing in Lokoja.

The Commission's federal commissioner for Kogi says it has established 4,011 functional registration centres across the 774 local government areas and is working towards about 8,000; the document does not say how many of them register on the platform. Undated, so the publication date is used.

The Commission describes VitalReg as giving 24-hour online access with records securely stored, and its ICT staff demonstrated a live birth registration on it that captures both parents' biodata and needs one parent's valid NIN to complete; where the entry is made is not stated. Undated, so the publication date is used.

The Commission's federal commissioner for Kogi says the platform is operated under a public-private partnership with Barnks-forte Technologies Ltd. as the Commission's technical partner, for availability, cybersecurity and continuing improvement; undated, so the publication date is used.

The National Population Commission commenced the registration, established the registration centres and is strengthening the capacity of its registration personnel; its Kogi director thanked the Federal Government, UNICEF and other development partners for supporting implementation. Undated, so the publication date is used.

systems.owner: National Population Commission (NPC); operated under a public-private partnership with Barnks-forte Technologies Ltd.
